identity.title: Strategic Navigation or Stochastic Search? How Agents and Humans Reason Over Document Collections

problem.claim: Determine whether multimodal agents reason strategically over document collections or rely on stochastic trial-and-error search.

gap.claim: Existing understanding lacks a direct account of agents' strategic behavior and its accuracy-effort trade-off in document-intensive search.

contributions.claim: MADQA, a benchmark containing 2,250 human-authored questions grounded in 800 heterogeneous PDF documents.
A protocol measuring the accuracy-effort trade-off to evaluate agentic behavior.
Release of the dataset and evaluation harness for studying efficient document retrieval and reasoning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce MADQA and describe the accuracy-effort evaluation protocol as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the best agents match human searchers in raw accuracy, but succeed on largely different questions.
The authors report that these agents rely on brute-force search to compensate for weak strategic planning and fail to close a nearly 20% gap to oracle performance.
The authors report that agents persist in unproductive loops.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames document-intensive automation as promising while questioning whether agents' behavior reflects strategic reasoning.
The authors introduce MADQA and use Classical Test Theory to target discriminative power across agentic-ability levels.
They introduce an accuracy-effort trade-off protocol for measuring agentic behavior.
They report human-level raw accuracy alongside different question success, brute-force compensation, a nearly 20% oracle gap, and release the dataset and harness.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs raw accuracy with effort, question overlap, planning behavior, and oracle-gap outcomes rather than treating accuracy alone as sufficient.

lessons.interpretation: This suggests that evaluations of search agents can expose behavioral differences hidden by aggregate accuracy.
lessons.application: Report accuracy together with effort, solved-question overlap, loop behavior, and an oracle-relative gap when assessing retrieval agents.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when effort is not measurable or when the task has no meaningful oracle or search trajectory.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify how effort, strategic planning, unproductive loops, or oracle performance are operationalized.
It does not provide numerical raw-accuracy results, statistical uncertainty, or details of the human and agent comparison samples.
